blocks.text: Keep one FormModel for field values, a FormUiState for navigation and interaction, a DraftEnvelope for durable local recovery, and a RemoteSaveState for optional synchronization. The two timestamps identify local durability and remote acknowledgement separately.

State-model checks:
- One form model spans every step.
- Dirty field paths identify edits captured by each save generation.
- schemaVersion governs client migration while baseRevision governs remote conflicts.
- lastLocalSavedAt and lastRemoteAcknowledgedAt communicate different facts.
- AbortController remains runtime state rather than serialized draft data.

blocks.title: Required fields
items: A single FormModel representing all 4 steps.
A currentStep value in UI state.
Dirty field paths that are cleared only for the save generation that captured them.
A validationErrors structure, not ad-hoc booleans everywhere.
A DraftEnvelope with schemaVersion, baseRevision, values, currentStep, dirtyPaths, and updatedAt.

blocks.title: Draft-model pitfalls
items: Scattering field values into many unrelated states instead of one model.
Encoding dirty state only implicitly (e.g. comparing JSON each time) instead of tracking it.
Storing huge, unstructured blobs in localStorage without a version field.
Mixing transient UI flags (loading spinners, focus) into the persisted draft.
Making the draft format inconsistent with the in-memory FormModel.

blocks.title: How the data typically evolves over time

steps.title: 1. Initialize form and save generations
steps.text: Form starts with a default FormModel (empty strings, defaults, etc.) and FormUiState with currentStep = 0, dirty = false, validationErrors = {}.

steps.title: 2. Advance one field generation
steps.text: An edit updates one field, marks its path dirty, and advances the local save generation. Blur may mark the field touched and derive a validation message.

steps.title: 3. Persist captured envelope
steps.text: The coordinator captures a DraftEnvelope, serializes it, and writes it atomically to local storage. Success updates lastLocalSavedAt and clears only unchanged paths captured by that generation; it does not update remote acknowledgement.

steps.title: 4. Resume from draft
steps.text: On return, the app parses and migrates the DraftEnvelope, compares its baseRevision with the optional remote draft, and restores or presents differences according to explicit authority rules.

items.label: Core model
items.helperText: Keeps user data and UI metadata clearly separated.

items.label: Persistence unit
items.helperText: The versioned recovery record written to the local repository.

items.label: Key concept
items.helperText: You always know whether the in-memory form matches the last persisted draft.

blocks.title: State checkpoint
blocks.text: A strong data model for this problem makes autosave almost trivial: one normalized form object, a small UI state wrapper, and a well-defined draft snapshot. If your types are clear, validation, dirty detection and serialization all fall into place.

Use a DraftEnvelope with schema version, base server version, updated timestamp, current step, field values, and dirty field paths. Keep validation results derived from values and submission attempt, not serialized as permanent truth. A pending save record stores generation, based-on version, and AbortController outside the value object.
